criteria.name: Artwork craft & genuine detail
criteria.notes: Real gains. 05's gallows is gone, and the empty mount reads at once as a camera mount with no camera: a flanged dome plate with bolt holes, a clamp collar, a base flange, and a cut cable with an orange taped end. The deck planks now have streaks along the grain. 06's lower band now carries a lit steel pool, and its boards sit larger and lower. 04's slab has a deeper front face and a feathered reflection. I can't find the old streak seam on 02's lid near x 750 (display). What still holds the score down: 05 is still clean vector illustration among PBR frames (01, 02, 09). Its ridges are flat silhouettes, the deck splits into two disagreeing planes with a dark strip and a dead black wedge at lower left, and the dark diagonal at lower right (about x 1300 to 1600, y 1600 to 1800 display) reads as a smear disconnected from the mount, which stands on the rail above it. 04, 06 and 07 still read as UI progress bars: flat white stock, flat colour fills, no tooth or bevel highlight. 06's orange top-face fill is an inset parallelogram that stops short of the front edge, and its head stops are two flat-shaded planes. 02's bumpers and body are still near-flat black. 08's tag and 03's foam remain the best 2D craft. The deck is a 7: strong in places, with three frames leaning on a default.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: This is still the predicted bail point, and the board still reads as a UI progress bar: flat white stock, a flat blue rectangle, uniform tick marks. The new front face is a grey gradient strip, and the feathered reflection is faint, so the slab has no material identity (no HDPE tooth, no bevel highlight).
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model the slab: a bright lit top arris, fine scored tooth on the top face, a front face that darkens with depth and carries the blue fill around the edge, and a sharper wet-steel reflection of the slab directly beneath it.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The boards are larger and lower, and the steel pool now fills the lower band, but they remain flat-fill slabs. The orange top-face fill is an inset parallelogram that stops about 30 px (display) short of the front edge, so it floats like a decal. The head stops are two flat-shaded planes with no arris or cast.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Run the top fill to the front edge so it meets the front-face fill on one depth line, give the head stops a lit bevel, a lee face and a cast onto the board, and add a surface tooth to the white stock.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The mount now reads correctly, but the frame is still clean vector illustration next to the PBR frames. The ridges are flat silhouettes. The deck breaks into two planes (a dark strip under the rail, then a lower planked deck) that don't agree. A dead black wedge fills the lower left, and the dark diagonal at lower right reads as a smear disconnected from the mount standing on the rail above.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Unify the near plane into one rail and deck surface on a single vanishing direction, ground the mount's cast shadow on the rail cap it actually stands on (delete the floating diagonal), and add atmospheric haze steps between ridge layers so they stop reading as cut paper.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Adding front faces didn't change the read. These are ten short, centred UI bars on black, identical in drawing to 04 and 06, and the cut board from 06 never arrives.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Draw the rows in 06's cabinet oblique, starting at the left edge with the same slab thickness and tick rhythm, so the first row visibly continues the board cut off at 06's right edge.
